title: NeuS: Learning Neural Implicit Surfaces by Volume Rendering for Multi-view Reconstruction
layout_note: Two captioned sub-figures split by a thin vertical rule: a narrow (a) schematic column on the left, itself split by a horizontal rule into a top and a bottom 1-D ray diagram, and a wide (b) strip of four same-pose renders (reference photo, two baselines, ours) labelled underneath.
grouping: Thin black rules separate (a) from (b) and the two rows of (a); each row of (a) has its rendering type written vertically along its left edge. (b) has no frames: four object renders at the same scale, each named underneath in a large serif label. Sub-figures are captioned (a)/(b) with a word.
shapes_depth: The (a) schematics are a 1-D side view of one camera ray: a blue camera glyph on the left, a dashed blue ray, and vertical bars for the scene (yellow) and the image (blue). The top row shows one grey dot on a dotted curved surface; the bottom row a row of grey sampled-point dots along the ray, with the bars made dotted and given a soft pink or light-blue glow. (b) renders are grey shaded meshes with no background, next to a colour reference photo.
proposed_highlight: The method's own result is the last render, labelled 'Ours', placed rightmost in the row of meshes; no colour or frame marks it, the clean surface does the work against the noisy baselines.
lesson: Contrast surface rendering and volume rendering as two stacked 1-D ray diagrams (camera, dashed ray, one hit point vs a row of sampled dots), then let a same-pose strip of grey mesh renders ending in 'Ours' carry the comparison.
notes: venue from the PDF first page footer 'NeurIPS 2021' (venue_source: pdf). Figures 2 and 3 could not be cropped (no caption found). Shaded mesh renders are raster content. Annotation note (2026-11-15): teaser rather than a full method figure: shows the rendering concept and a result comparison, not the network

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: surface rendering and volume rendering drawn as two stacked ray diagrams in (a), and IDR, NeRF and Ours meshes as a same-pose strip in (b) with ours last

relations.form: (b) is a strip of four same-pose renders left to right: reference photo, IDR mesh, NeRF mesh, Ours mesh, labelled below
(a) stacks a 'surface rendering' row over a 'volume rendering' row, split by a horizontal rule, each a 1-D side view with the same camera, ray and image-bar vocabulary
each (a) row draws the operation on one ray: surface rendering hits one grey dot on a dotted curved surface, volume rendering places a row of grey sampled-point dots along the ray
the reference photo leads the (b) strip so each mesh is compared against it by adjacency

channels.colour: blue = camera, ray and image bar; yellow = scene objects; glow tint around bars in volume rendering marks contributions from all samples; (b) uses grey shading for all meshes and colour only for the reference photo
channels.shape: dot = a point evaluated on the ray; bar = an image plane or object slice
channels.line: dashed blue = camera ray; dotted curve = implicit surface; dotted bars in volume rendering = soft, accumulated content
channels.frame: a thin vertical rule separates (a) from (b), a horizontal rule separates the two (a) rows; no boxes

quality.strengths: The (b) strip compares the alternatives as identical same-pose renders with ours last, letting the wavy interior of IDR and striped walls of NeRF be seen directly; the (a) rows reuse one camera/ray/bar vocabulary so the only difference is one hit point versus many samples.
quality.weaknesses: The method itself (the SDF-to-weight volume rendering that is NeuS's contribution) is not drawn; (a) is a cramped narrow column with vertical rotated labels and tiny glyphs while most of the area goes to result renders; ours carries no highlight beyond position.

insights.structure: A narrow (a) column on the left, split by a horizontal rule into a 'surface rendering' row and a 'volume rendering' row (labels written vertically on the left edge), is separated by a thin vertical rule from a wide (b) strip of four same-pose renders: reference photo, IDR, NeRF, Ours.
insights.data: Each (a) row is a 1-D side view of one ray: blue camera glyph, dashed blue ray, yellow scene bars and a blue image bar; surface rendering shows one grey hit dot on a dotted curved surface, volume rendering a row of grey sampled-point dots with glowing dotted bars; (b) shows a colour photo then grey shaded meshes on white.
insights.emphasis: 'Ours' is simply the rightmost mesh in the strip; its clean walls versus IDR's wavy interior and NeRF's noisy stripes carry the claim with no highlight colour or frame.
insights.flow: Read (a) top to bottom (surface vs volume), then (b) left to right from reference image to baselines to ours; the only arrows are the camera rays pointing right.
insights.avoid: The two halves are only loosely linked: the (a) schematic is tiny and its labels ('surface', 'sampled points') are small compared with the large (b) renders, and the comparison to two baselines carries no indication of what is wrong with them.

arrangement.units: two unframed sub-figures split by a thin vertical rule, captioned '(a) Illustration' and '(b) Example' below; (a) is internally split by a horizontal rule into two ray-diagram rows
arrangement.inputs_as: the reference photo leftmost in (b); camera glyphs at the left of each (a) row
